exposure: Insulin strategy based on maternal capillary blood glucose (CBG) thresholds (MG group)
Insulin strategy based on fetal abdominal circumference >=75th percentile and CBG safety levels (FG group)
cohort: The study included 46 pregnant women with GCK-MODY, divided into two groups based on their chosen insulin treatment strategy.
finding: The rate of large for gestational age (LGA) neonates primarily depended on the fetal GCK genotype (0% in GCK variant vs 36% in those without) rather than the treatment strategy or glycaemic management.
mod_finding: The rate of Caesarean sections in the total cohort was 40%, but no associations were found between C-section rates and pregnancy characteristics, insulin therapy strategy, or glycaemic management.
birth_weight: Babies classified as large for gestational age (LGA) were included, implying a focus on birth weight relative to gestational age, but no specific weight ranges were provided.
gest_age: Babies classified as preterm deliveries (rate 2.2%) and large for gestational age (LGA) were included, implying consideration of gestational age.
